| [r1 — The GRU's latents carry the GLM-HMM's state posterior at every K, beyond engagement (training mice)](r1-pilot-decoding.md) | draft: claims check and first-author review pending | Study 02's 3-way GRU was trained only to predict the next choice; study 14's GLM-HMM explains the same trials with K discrete states. Does the GRU's hidden state contain, in linearly readable form, the GLM-HMM's belief about which state the mouse is in, beyond what the GRU's own prediction and simple choice and reward history carry? If it does, the expressive model and the interpretable one describe the same behavioural variables, and the GLM-HMM's states can be used to read the GRU. | **F1.** At every K from 2 to 10, a linear readout of the GRU latents recovers the GLM-HMM's predictive state posterior on mice it never saw (pooled R² at least 0.82 [0.80, 0.83] and within session at least 0.72 [0.70, 0.73], both lowest at K = 9; 95% intervals over n = 50 mice), while the GRU's own logits and linear history fall to 0.25 [0.21, 0.28] and 0.28 [0.24, 0.32] at K = 10.<br>**F2.** The decoded state is more than engagement: on engaged trials at K = 3, the latents separate the two engaged states (S1 vs S2 R² 0.88 [0.86, 0.90]), while the GRU's logits and linear history recover at most 0.07 and 0.06 of it (upper 95% bounds; points 0.03 and 0.00; n = 50 mice).<br>**F3.** The decoding follows this session's state at this moment: within session the latents score 0.72 to 0.88 (K = 2, 3, 6, 10; intervals in the Fig. 3 table), while every within-session null of the latents decoder (session swap, circular shift) stays at or below 0.04 (5 to 10 shuffles per cell).<br>**F4.** Decoding does not single out a number of states: the latents' pooled R² is highest at K = 2 and is 0.09 [0.08, 0.10] lower at K = 10 than at K = 3 (paired 95% interval over n = 50 mice), so r1 shows shared variables, not a preferred number of discrete states. |
